json.summary: The JSON Formatter helps developers inspect API responses, logs, configuration snippets, and pasted JSON samples without changing the source data.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it when an API response is hard to read, when a configuration file needs consistent indentation, or when a JSON sample must be checked before it is shared in documentation.
The formatter keeps valid values intact. It changes whitespace for readability or removes whitespace for compact output.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: Input: {"status":"ok","items":[{"id":1,"name":"sample"}]}
Formatted output uses nested indentation so object keys, arrays, and values can be reviewed line by line.

sections.heading: Common validation errors
paragraphs: Strict JSON does not allow trailing commas, comments, single-quoted strings, or unquoted object keys.
If pasted API output fails validation, confirm that the response is not an HTML error page, JSONP wrapper, or log prefix.

sections.heading: Privacy boundary
paragraphs: Do not paste passwords, production tokens, private keys, customer records, or confidential payloads into browser tools unless your own security process allows it.

faqs.question: Does formatting change the JSON values?
faqs.answer: No. Formatting changes whitespace only after the input has parsed as valid JSON.

faqs.question: Why does valid JavaScript object syntax fail?
faqs.answer: JSON is stricter than JavaScript object literals. Keys and string values need double quotes, and comments are not valid JSON.

base64.summary: The Base64 Encoder and Decoder converts text to Base64 and decodes Base64 back to readable UTF-8 text for transport and documentation checks.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it for small text payloads, examples in API documentation, test fixtures, and configuration values that need Base64 representation.
Base64 is an encoding format. It is not encryption and should not be used as access control.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: Input text: Ymir Tool
Base64 output: WW1pciBUb29s

sections.heading: Common decode errors
paragraphs: Decode can fail when the string has invalid characters, missing padding, URL-safe substitutions, or binary bytes that are not valid UTF-8 text.

sections.heading: Privacy boundary
paragraphs: Do not treat Base64 as secret storage. Anyone who receives the encoded string can decode it.

faqs.question: Is Base64 secure?
faqs.answer: No. Base64 is reversible encoding, not encryption.

faqs.question: Can it handle Chinese characters?
faqs.answer: Yes. The tool should encode and decode UTF-8 text, including Chinese characters and emoji.

md5.summary: The MD5 Hash Generator creates deterministic MD5 digests for quick comparisons, sample data checks, and legacy checksum workflows.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it to compare two text snippets, verify that copied sample data has not changed, or reproduce a legacy system checksum during debugging.
MD5 is fast and widely recognized, but it is not collision resistant enough for modern security decisions.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: Input text: Ymir Tool
The output is a 32-character hexadecimal digest that should remain identical for the same input bytes.

sections.heading: Important security limit
paragraphs: Do not store passwords with plain MD5. Password storage should use a dedicated password hashing algorithm with salt and work factors.
For file integrity or security-sensitive verification, use a stronger checksum or signature workflow required by your project.

faqs.question: Can MD5 prove that content is authentic?
faqs.answer: No. MD5 can help spot accidental changes, but it does not prove authenticity against an attacker.

faqs.question: Why does whitespace change the hash?
faqs.answer: Hash functions process exact bytes. A space, newline, or different character encoding changes the digest.

formatjs.summary: The JavaScript Formatter turns minified or compact JavaScript into readable indentation and can prepare small snippets for review.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it when a bundled snippet, bookmarklet, console sample, or documentation example needs readable line breaks before review.
Formatting is a readability step. It should not be treated as a security review or code execution sandbox.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: Input: function demo(){return [1,2,3].map(x=>x*2)}
Formatted output separates blocks, callbacks, arrays, and return statements so the control flow is easier to scan.

sections.heading: Common caveats
paragraphs: Broken JavaScript, incomplete copied fragments, or template syntax from another framework may not format as expected.
Do not paste proprietary production bundles unless your internal policy allows browser-based formatting.

faqs.question: Does this execute the JavaScript?
faqs.answer: No. Formatting should parse and rearrange text; it should not run pasted code.

faqs.question: Can formatting change behavior?
faqs.answer: A formatter should preserve behavior, but always review the result before copying it into source control.

textdiff.summary: The Text Diff tool compares two blocks of text line by line so edits, removals, and additions are easier to inspect before copying.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it to compare configuration drafts, translation changes, release notes, log excerpts, documentation revisions, or two copied command outputs.
Line-by-line diff is best for text where line breaks carry meaning. For binary files or very large files, use a dedicated version control diff.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: Text A: JSON Formatter and Base64 Encoder
Text B: JSON Formatter and Text Diff. The result highlights the changed line so the replacement is easy to review.

sections.heading: Review workflow
paragraphs: Paste the older text on the left and the newer text on the right. Review added, removed, and changed lines before copying any merged result.
Whitespace, punctuation, and casing differences can matter, especially for config files and command examples.

faqs.question: Can this merge two versions automatically?
faqs.answer: No. It helps identify differences. You should decide how to merge the content.

faqs.question: Why do unchanged-looking lines show as changed?
faqs.answer: Hidden whitespace, different punctuation, or different line endings can cause a line to compare differently.

txtcount.summary: The Word Counter measures characters, words, lines, paragraphs, and byte length for writing limits, metadata drafts, and translation checks.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it to check SEO titles, meta descriptions, social posts, product copy, translation strings, form limits, and short documentation snippets.
Character count and byte count are different. Non-ASCII text can use more bytes than visible characters depending on encoding.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: Input: Free online developer tools
The summary reports visible characters, words, and line counts so the draft can be adjusted before publishing.

sections.heading: Counting notes
paragraphs: Whitespace, emoji, punctuation, and line breaks can affect totals. For strict platform limits, paste the final text exactly as it will be submitted.
For multilingual text, use the character count as the primary limit check and the word count as a rough guide.

faqs.question: Why is byte count larger than character count?
faqs.answer: UTF-8 uses multiple bytes for many non-English characters and emoji.

faqs.question: Should spaces count?
faqs.answer: Most platform limits count spaces as characters, so this tool includes them in character totals.

regex.summary: The Regex Tester checks regular expression patterns against sample text so matches, groups, and flags can be reviewed before use.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it to test validation patterns, log filters, text extraction rules, replacement drafts, and documentation examples with realistic sample input.
A pattern that works on one sample may still fail on real data. Test positive cases, negative cases, and edge cases.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: Pattern: \b\w+@\w+\.com\b
Sample text with an email-like value should show the matched substring and make escaping mistakes easier to find.

sections.heading: Performance caution
paragraphs: Nested quantifiers and broad wildcards can cause slow matching on long text. Keep patterns specific when they will run on production input.
Always escape user-provided text before embedding it inside a regular expression.

faqs.question: Why does a backslash disappear?
faqs.answer: Some programming languages require string escaping before the regex engine sees the pattern.

faqs.question: Can one regex validate every email address?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. Use a practical pattern for UI checks and server-side validation for real workflows.

calculator.summary: The Scientific Calculator evaluates common arithmetic expressions for quick checks, estimates, and small calculation workflows.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it for quick arithmetic, unit-adjacent estimates, percentage checks, exponent calculations, and verifying numbers before copying them into a document.
For financial, engineering, medical, or legal decisions, verify the result with the authoritative calculator or source required by that workflow.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: The output should evaluate the expression and let you copy the numeric result after checking operator precedence.

sections.heading: Calculation notes
paragraphs: Decimal arithmetic in browsers can show floating-point rounding behavior. Round final results according to your actual use case.
Write expressions clearly with parentheses when a result depends on order of operations.

faqs.question: Why do some decimal results have many digits?
faqs.answer: JavaScript and most browser calculators use binary floating-point numbers, which can expose tiny rounding differences.

faqs.question: Can this replace a spreadsheet?
faqs.answer: No. Use it for quick checks, not for audited models or repeatable business calculations.

unixtime.summary: The Unix Timestamp Converter changes timestamps into readable dates and converts dates back into timestamp values for debugging and documentation.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it when logs, API payloads, database fields, or webhook events contain Unix timestamps that need a quick human-readable date.
It is especially useful when checking whether a value is in seconds, milliseconds, or an ISO date format.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: The output should show the corresponding date and time using the selected timezone or the browser's local timezone.

sections.heading: Seconds vs milliseconds
paragraphs: Ten-digit Unix timestamps are usually seconds. Thirteen-digit values are usually milliseconds.
If a converted date is thousands of years away, the value was probably interpreted with the wrong unit.

faqs.question: Why does my teammate see a different time?
faqs.answer: The same timestamp can display differently in different timezones. Compare UTC when you need a shared reference.

faqs.question: Does a Unix timestamp include timezone data?
faqs.answer: No. The timestamp represents a point in time; timezone affects only how that point is displayed.

urlencode.summary: The URL Encoder and Decoder converts reserved characters to percent-encoded text and decodes encoded URL parts for inspection.

sections.heading: When this tool is useful
paragraphs: Use it when query parameters, redirect URLs, callback values, search strings, or copied links need to be encoded safely for transport.
Encode only the component that needs encoding. Encoding an entire URL can change separators such as colon, slash, question mark, and ampersand.

sections.heading: Input and output example
paragraphs: Input query value: Ymir Tool JSON
Encoded value: Ymir%20Tool%20JSON

sections.heading: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Double-encoding turns percent signs into %25 and can break callbacks or redirect parameters.
Plus signs and spaces are handled differently in some form-encoded query strings, so verify the target system's expected format.

faqs.question: Should I encode the whole URL?
faqs.answer: Usually no. Encode parameter values or path segments separately unless the target system asks for an encoded full URL.

faqs.question: Why did % become %25?
faqs.answer: That usually means already encoded text was encoded a second time.
